findings.title: graph_resume_ask idempotency is process-local: a landed request replayed from a fresh host (empty dispatcher mirror) returns Err
findings.detail: The is_landed early-return lives behind `ask_dispatcher.pending_request(request_id)`, so it only fires when this process still holds the (Consumed) mirror entry. A second host process/restart sharing the same sessions.db + graph store gets `Err("unknown control request")` for the same already-landed request instead of `{resumed:false, landed:"already_landed"}`. No data loss: the durable record is landed, the run is Ready and the injection is queued; only the retry-after-restart response shape differs. Out of the round-3 counter-example scope (same-process double resume), so non-blocking.

findings.title: Sweep-rebuilt injection stamps post-transition version, live answer path stamps pre-transition version
findings.detail: answer_ask_in_session -> build_session_injection(answered_version = expected_version); sweep_unlanded_answer_landings -> build_session_injection(record.version) where record.version is already expected+1. terminalResult.output.version is therefore 1 on the live path and 2 on the rebuilt path for the same request. Display-only field, no consumer validates it, but the two landings are not byte-identical.

findings.title: A JSON-null answer is delivered live but is indistinguishable from a missing payload for the sweep (would strand the record unlanded)
findings.detail: answer_json stores the literal `null`, and load_unlanded_answered_payloads maps it to Value::Null, which the sweep treats as `missing_durable_answer` and skips. Live path: answer_ask_in_session(json!(null)) queues an injection with answer:null and marks it landed, so the failure only surfaces if that landing write fails (or the bound resume never happens): the record then stays unlanded forever and the answer is never delivered. Fail-closed is consistent with the 'never rebuild with null' rule, but the entry accepts an answer payload it cannot replay.

falsification_attempts.evidence: Fresh probe crate /tmp/l3f4-ask (links pony-agent-core by path, no repo writes). `cargo run -q -- r4-payload`: real entry `answer_ask_in_session("session-A", req, 1, "继续执行-REAL-4F9C")` on a graph-bound Ask returned Ok(lifecycleState=answered, landed=resume); [R1.durable_payload] = Ok([(PersistedAsk{state:Answered, version:2, ...}, String("继续执行-REAL-4F9C"))]) i.e. answer_json already durable while landed_at_ms is still NULL; a fresh host with an EMPTY injection queue rebuilt exactly 1 record: [R1.sweep_rebuilt] 1, [R1.rebuilt_terminal_result] output.answer = "继续执行-REAL-4F9C", [R1.rebuilt_answer_equals_user_choice] Some(true), [R1.rebuilt_serialized] contains no rebuiltFromDurable/placeholder/stub/null, [R1.landed_after_sweep] Ok(true). End-to-end: next turn's provider body carries the same real answer ([R1.provider_body_carries_real_answer] Some(true), [R1.provider_body_has_placeholder] Some([])). Atomicity is code-verified: transition_scoped_inner opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE, applies the state UPDATE and the answer_json UPDATE, then commits (ask_persistence.rs:399-435) — no window where Answered exists without its payload. A direct-CAS (no payload) record is skipped rather than rebuilt from a placeholder (`r4` precursor `cargo run -q -- rebuild` -> 'answer landing sweep skipped request=... reason=missing_durable_answer', queue stays empty).

`cargo run -q -- r4-landed` (real graph run + mock provider + file-backed sessions.db): bound Ask answered -> [R2.answer_landing] Ok(landed="resume"), [R2.landed_after_answer] Ok(false), [R2.unlanded_after_answer] Ok(1), [R2.queue_after_answer] [] (nothing marked landed, nothing queued before resume). Stale resume -> [R2.stale_resume] Err("bound at version 1 but resume presented version 6"), [R2.landed_after_failed_resume] Ok(false), [R2.unlanded_after_failed_resume] Ok(1), [R2.run_phase_after_failed_resume] Some("waiting_user") — failure keeps it retryable. Sweep retried with the binding's own version: [R2.sweep] 1, [R2.landed_after_sweep] Ok(true), [R2.run_phase_after_sweep] Some("ready"), binding consumed. Idempotent replay: [R2.resume_after_landed] Ok({resumed:false, landed:"already_landed"}) and again on the second call — no Err. Non-bound landing reports the queue variant ([R3.answer_after_failed_gc] Ok((answered, landed="queue"))). Residual scope gap recorded as ADVISORY R4-ADV-1 (fresh-host replay hits the missing mirror before the is_landed check).

`cargo run -q -- r4-gc-fail` (full-delegation FailGcStore whose only failure is gc_orphans; archived session owns one pending Ask): [R3.expire] {orphaned:0, reclaimed:0} + log 'gc_orphan_asks failed; mirror left untouched'; [R3.disk_after_failed_gc] Some((1, Pending)) AND [R3.mirror_after_failed_gc] Some((1, Pending)), [R3.list_after_failed_gc] Some(1). Functional consequence probe: the still-pending record is answerable through the real entry ([R3.answer_after_failed_gc] Ok((answered, queue)), disk (2,Answered), mirror (2,Consumed)) — i.e. the round-3 fork (mirror terminally closed on disk failure) is gone. Mirror close is gated on `durable_written` (ask_plan_commands.rs:571-600); expire_asks' second half only reconciles Approval TTL (dispatcher.rs:1003-1022), so it cannot fork an Interaction.

`cargo run -q -- r4-retention` (file-backed store): direct guard — [R4.gc_direct_reclaimed] Ok(3) deleting only answered+landed / cancelled / superseded; survivors: req-pending Some(Pending), req-unlanded Some(Answered) (state=answered, landed_at_ms IS NULL) — never reclaimed, while req-landed/req-cancelled/req-superseded are None. Real host entry — seeded an Answered row landed 8 days ago plus an old unlanded Answered and a 30-day-old Pending, then `plane.expire_asks(Some(now))`: [R4.expire_first] reclaimed=1, [R4.expire_second] reclaimed=0 (no spin, no repeat), [R4.plane_survivor_req-old-landed] None / req-old-unlanded Some((2,Answered)) / req-old-pending Some((1,Pending)). Matches ask_persistence.rs:869-882 (`state <> 'pending' AND NOT (state='answered' AND landed_at_ms IS NULL) AND COALESCE(landed_at_ms, answered_at_ms, created_at_ms) < ?1`).
